subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hale and hearty
solution:
The correct answer is **'Strong and healthy'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The meaning of the idiom **'Hale and hearty'** is **'Strong and healthy'.**

 
 
• **E.g.**__- She is still **hale and hearty** in her nineties.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **'Strong and healthy'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• The term **'hale and hearty'** derives from Old English, the language spoken in England prior to the late 11th century. In Old English, the word **'hal'** means **'safe'** or **'unhurt'**. It is the root word of the modern English words '**whole'** and '**heal'** as well as **'health'** and '**hail'**. The modern English word '**hale'** meaning **fit and healthy**, derives from this root.
 
• The word '**hearty'** first appears in the 14th century and is used to mean '**spirited'** or '**courageous'**. In the Middle Ages, the heart was thought to be the seat of feelings. As a result, a wide variety of English terms refer to the heart in this way. Examples include '**hard-hearted'**, **heartfelt'** and '**heartbreak'**. To be '**hearty'**, therefore, is **to have a strong heart and to be in high spirits.**
